hook.text: The sun delivers 10,000 times more energy than humanity uses — nano is key to capturing more of it efficiently.

buildup.text: Nanomaterials offer huge surface areas, tunable bandgaps, and quantum effects that bulk materials lack.

discovery.text: These properties accelerate charge transfer, boost light absorption, and enable new energy conversion pathways.

twist.text: Scaling nano from lab to factory is expensive — manufacturing cost often erases the efficiency gains.

climax.text: Roll-to-roll printing and solution processing are cutting costs — nano energy devices are reaching market scale.

punchline.text: Nano turns abundant sunlight into affordable electricity — surface by surface.

quiz.question: Why do nanomaterials improve energy devices?
options: They are heavier and store more energy
High surface areas, tunable bandgaps, and quantum effects enhance energy conversion
They reflect light better than bulk materials

hook.text: Tune a quantum dot's size and change which color of sunlight it absorbs — one material, infinite bandgaps.

buildup.text: Colloidal QDs are printed onto flexible substrates — creating solar cells cheaply from a liquid ink.

discovery.text: Multiple exciton generation lets one photon create two electron-hole pairs — potentially exceeding the Shockley-Queisser limit.

twist.text: Surface defects trap charges before extraction — passivation chemistry is critical to efficiency and stability.

climax.text: QD solar cell efficiency reached 18.1% in 2023 — approaching commercial viability after years of lab progress.

punchline.text: Print tiny dots on a sheet and harvest sunlight at any color.

quiz.question: What is multiple exciton generation in quantum dot solar cells?
options: One photon creates two or more electron-hole pairs, potentially exceeding standard efficiency limits
Multiple photons combine to excite one electron to a higher state
Excitons from adjacent dots merge into a stronger current

hook.text: In 2009, perovskite solar cells were 3.8% efficient — by 2024 they hit 33.9% in tandem with silicon.

buildup.text: Halide perovskites absorb light in layers just 500 nm thick — a hundred times thinner than silicon wafers.

discovery.text: Solution processing at low temperatures means cheap fabrication — no billion-dollar clean rooms needed.

twist.text: Perovskites degrade in moisture, heat, and UV — stability remains the biggest barrier to commercialization.

climax.text: Encapsulation and 2D-3D heterostructures now extend lifetimes to years — several companies plan mass production.

punchline.text: A nano-thin crystal film rivals decades of silicon engineering.

quiz.question: What is the main challenge preventing perovskite solar cell commercialization?
options: They cannot absorb enough sunlight
Degradation from moisture, heat, and UV reduces long-term stability
They require extremely expensive raw materials

hook.text: A sponge of TiO₂ nanoparticles coated in dye absorbs light like a leaf — the Grätzel cell mimics photosynthesis.

buildup.text: Dye molecules inject excited electrons into the nano-TiO₂ scaffold — the porous structure provides enormous surface area.

discovery.text: DSSCs work in diffuse light and at wide angles — outperforming silicon indoors and on cloudy days.

twist.text: Liquid electrolyte can leak and evaporate — solid-state alternatives exist but reduce efficiency.

climax.text: Indoor DSSC panels now power IoT sensors in offices — harvesting ambient light that silicon cells ignore.

punchline.text: A nano sponge soaked in dye turns indoor light into power.

quiz.question: Why do dye-sensitized solar cells outperform silicon indoors?
options: They are more transparent
Their dye molecules absorb diffuse light efficiently at wide angles
They use less silicon material

hook.text: A forest of vertical nanowires traps light like a black hole — absorbing more sunlight than a flat surface.

buildup.text: Light bounces between nanowires, getting multiple absorption chances — anti-reflection is built into the geometry.

discovery.text: Each nanowire is a radial p-n junction — carriers travel short distances to the junction, reducing recombination.

twist.text: Surface recombination on the huge nanowire surface area fights against the short-diffusion advantage.

climax.text: InP nanowire solar cells reached 17.8% efficiency — proving nanowire geometry can compete with planar designs.

punchline.text: A forest of nano pillars traps light and converts it all.

quiz.question: How do nanowire solar cells improve light absorption?
options: The wires emit their own light to supplement sunlight
Light bounces between vertical wires, getting multiple absorption chances
They reflect light back to the sun to warm it further

hook.text: Stack two different absorbers and each catches a different part of the spectrum — tandem cells break 30% efficiency.

buildup.text: A perovskite top cell absorbs blue-green light while silicon below catches the red-infrared remainder.

discovery.text: Nano-textured interfaces between layers scatter and trap light — maximizing absorption in both sub-cells.

twist.text: Current matching between the two cells is critical — if one produces less, it limits the whole tandem.

climax.text: LONGi's perovskite-silicon tandem reached 33.9% in 2023 — the highest certified efficiency for any two-junction cell.

punchline.text: Two nano-thin layers capture what one layer alone would waste.

quiz.question: Why do tandem solar cells achieve higher efficiency?
options: They use twice as much silicon
Each layer absorbs a different part of the solar spectrum, reducing thermalization losses
They operate at higher temperatures

hook.text: Silicon stores ten times more lithium than graphite — but it swells 300% and cracks. Nano solves this.

buildup.text: Silicon nanoparticles and nanowires accommodate swelling without fracturing — small structures flex instead of breaking.

discovery.text: Nano-structured silicon anodes boost battery capacity from 372 to over 3000 mAh per gram of anode material.

twist.text: Continuous SEI formation on fresh silicon surfaces consumes electrolyte — capacity fades after hundreds of cycles.

climax.text: Engineered carbon-silicon core-shell nanoparticles now stabilize the SEI — commercial SiO anodes are in EV batteries.

punchline.text: Nano silicon flexes instead of cracking — unlocking ten times the capacity.

quiz.question: Why does nano-structured silicon solve the swelling problem in battery anodes?
options: Nanoparticles do not absorb lithium
Small structures accommodate volume expansion without fracturing
Silicon nanoparticles repel lithium ions to prevent swelling

hook.text: Liquid electrolytes leak and burn — solid nano-ceramic electrolytes eliminate fire risk in lithium batteries.

buildup.text: Thin ceramic films like LLZO conduct lithium ions through vacancies in their crystalline lattice.

discovery.text: Nano-grained ceramics have more grain boundaries — fast ion diffusion paths that boost conductivity.

twist.text: Grain boundaries are also where lithium dendrites nucleate — the very paths that help conduction enable shorts.

climax.text: Toyota plans to ship solid-state batteries by 2027 — promising double the range and ten-minute charging.

punchline.text: Replace liquid with a nano ceramic and batteries stop catching fire.

quiz.question: Why are nanostructured ceramic electrolytes promising for batteries?
options: They store more lithium in their crystal structure
Grain boundaries provide fast ion diffusion paths and the solid form eliminates flammability
They are transparent, allowing visual inspection of the battery

hook.text: Sulfur is cheap and holds five times more energy than lithium-ion cathodes — but it dissolves away during cycling.

buildup.text: Polysulfide intermediates dissolve in the electrolyte and shuttle between electrodes — killing capacity fast.

discovery.text: Porous carbon nano-hosts trap polysulfides inside — confining them physically and adsorbing them chemically.

twist.text: Sulfur is an insulator — the carbon host must also provide electronic conductivity to the trapped sulfur.

climax.text: Nano-MXene hosts combine conductivity and polysulfide binding — pushing cycle life past 1000 cycles.

punchline.text: Trap sulfur in a nano cage and batteries hold five times more energy.

quiz.question: How do nano carbon hosts improve lithium-sulfur batteries?
options: They increase the sulfur content beyond the theoretical limit
They physically and chemically trap polysulfides, preventing shuttle degradation
They replace sulfur as the active material

hook.text: Charge a phone in five minutes — nano-sized cathode particles shorten the distance lithium ions must travel.

buildup.text: In bulk cathodes, ions diffuse micrometers to reach the center — in nano cathodes, the path is just nanometers.

discovery.text: LiFePO₄ nanoparticles charge in seconds per particle — the rate limit shifts to electronic wiring, not ion diffusion.

twist.text: Nano particles pack less densely — volumetric energy density drops even as rate capability improves.

climax.text: Carbon-coated nano-LFP is now the dominant EV battery chemistry in China — safe, fast, and affordable.

punchline.text: Shrink the cathode particle and charging time shrinks with it.

quiz.question: Why do nano-sized cathode particles enable fast charging?
options: They have higher voltage than bulk particles
Shorter diffusion distances let lithium ions enter and exit the particle much faster
They eliminate the need for an electrolyte

hook.text: Sodium is 1000 times more abundant than lithium — nano electrodes make sodium-ion batteries finally competitive.

buildup.text: Sodium ions are larger than lithium — they need wider diffusion channels that nanostructured hosts provide.

discovery.text: Hard carbon nanospheres with tunable pore sizes intercalate sodium efficiently — reaching 300 mAh per gram.

twist.text: Sodium batteries are heavier per kWh than lithium — they suit stationary storage better than electric vehicles.

climax.text: CATL ships sodium-ion batteries for grid storage — nano-engineered electrodes make cheap abundant elements viable.

punchline.text: Nano channels in carbon welcome the bigger sodium ion — cheap energy storage arrives.

quiz.question: Why do sodium-ion batteries need nanostructured electrodes?
options: Sodium ions are smaller and need tighter confinement
Larger sodium ions require wider diffusion channels that nanostructured hosts provide
Sodium reacts violently with bulk materials

hook.text: Lithium dendrites grow like metal trees through the battery — they short-circuit and cause fires.

buildup.text: Uneven lithium deposition on the anode creates needle-like growths that pierce the separator membrane.

discovery.text: Nano-porous scaffolds distribute lithium evenly — the metal fills pores uniformly instead of growing sharp tips.

twist.text: At high charging rates, dendrites can still form between scaffold pores — rate limits persist despite nano design.

climax.text: Artificial SEI layers made of nano-ceramic particles now suppress dendrites through 500+ cycles in prototypes.

punchline.text: A nano scaffold tames lithium's wild growth — batteries get safer.

quiz.question: How do nano-porous scaffolds prevent lithium dendrites?
options: They block all lithium from reaching the anode
They distribute lithium deposition evenly, preventing sharp needle-like growths
They dissolve dendrites as they form

hook.text: Charge in seconds, discharge in seconds — supercapacitors with graphene electrodes deliver instant power bursts.

buildup.text: Graphene's theoretical surface area is 2630 m² per gram — ions line up on both sides of every single-atom sheet.

discovery.text: Laser-scribed graphene creates porous 3D structures from graphite oxide — a simple, scalable process.

twist.text: Graphene sheets restack during processing — reducing the accessible surface and killing capacitance.

climax.text: Spacer nanoparticles between sheets prevent restacking — maintaining high surface area in practical devices.

punchline.text: A single-atom sheet stores energy on both sides — instant power from a carbon lattice.

quiz.question: Why is graphene ideal for supercapacitor electrodes?
options: It stores energy in chemical bonds like a battery
Its enormous surface area allows ions to line up on both sides of each atomic sheet
It generates electricity when exposed to light

hook.text: MXenes are 2D sheets of metal carbides — conductive as metals, with surface chemistry that grabs ions.

buildup.text: Ti₃C₂Tₓ layers intercalate ions between sheets — combining battery-like capacity with supercapacitor speed.

discovery.text: MXene films achieve volumetric capacitance over 1500 F/cm³ — the highest for any 2D material.

twist.text: MXenes oxidize in air and water — shelf life without inert storage is measured in weeks.

climax.text: Sealed MXene micro-supercapacitors on chips power wireless sensors — nano energy storage for IoT devices.

punchline.text: A metal carbide sheet stores energy fast and dense — if you keep it from air.

quiz.question: What gives MXenes their high volumetric capacitance?
options: They are the lightest materials known
Metallic conductivity combined with surface-driven ion intercalation between dense 2D layers
They store energy as heat rather than charge

hook.text: Batteries are slow but store a lot — capacitors are fast but store little. Pseudocapacitors do both.

buildup.text: Surface redox reactions at nanostructured oxide electrodes store charge — faradaic but capacitor-fast.

discovery.text: RuO₂ nanoparticles show near-ideal pseudocapacitance — 900 F/g with no diffusion limitation at nanoscale.

twist.text: Ruthenium is rare and expensive — MnO₂ and Fe₃O₄ nano alternatives trade some performance for affordability.

climax.text: Hybrid devices pair a pseudocapacitive electrode with a battery electrode — capturing both speed and energy.

punchline.text: Surface chemistry at nanoscale bridges the gap between batteries and capacitors.

quiz.question: What is pseudocapacitance?
options: Charge storage that only works at cryogenic temperatures
Fast surface redox reactions at nanostructured electrodes that store charge like a battery at capacitor speed
Capacitance created by stacking multiple capacitors in series

hook.text: A supercapacitor thinner than a human hair sits on a microchip — powering a sensor from its own tiny reservoir.

buildup.text: Interdigitated finger electrodes patterned by lithography maximize edge length in minimal area.

discovery.text: Carbon nanotube or graphene forests grown between the fingers provide huge surface area in microns of height.

twist.text: Electrolyte choices for on-chip use are limited — gel and solid electrolytes avoid leakage but have lower conductivity.

climax.text: Integrated micro-supercapacitors now pair with energy harvesters — self-powered IoT chips that never need batteries.

punchline.text: Shrink the supercapacitor onto the chip and the chip powers itself.

quiz.question: Why are micro-supercapacitors valuable for IoT devices?
options: They replace the processor on the chip
They store energy on-chip for burst power, enabling battery-free self-powered sensor nodes
They transmit data faster than conventional chips

hook.text: Bend it, stretch it, twist it — a nanofiber supercapacitor woven into fabric stores energy while you move.

buildup.text: Carbon nanofiber yarns coated with MnO₂ act as electrodes — twisted into threads that conduct and store.

discovery.text: These fiber supercapacitors survive 10,000 bending cycles without losing capacitance — truly wearable energy.

twist.text: Energy density per meter of fiber is still low — you would need meters of fiber for meaningful storage.

climax.text: Textile-integrated energy storage powers LED displays woven into sportswear — fashion meets nano energy.

punchline.text: Weave a supercapacitor into your shirt and wear your power source.

quiz.question: What enables flexible supercapacitors to survive bending?
options: They are made of rigid ceramics that resist deformation
Nanofiber yarn electrodes maintain electrical contact and structure through thousands of bending cycles
They contain liquid mercury that flows during bending

hook.text: Use a different material for each electrode and the voltage window doubles — asymmetric supercapacitors store more.

buildup.text: One electrode uses carbon for capacitive storage; the other uses a metal oxide for faradaic pseudo-capacitance.

discovery.text: The wider voltage window increases energy density by the square of voltage — a huge gain from one change.

twist.text: Balancing charge between two different electrodes is tricky — mass ratio and kinetics must match precisely.

climax.text: Nano-MnO₂ paired with activated carbon reaches energy densities rivaling some batteries — with capacitor-speed charge.

punchline.text: Two different nano electrodes double the voltage and quadruple the energy.

quiz.question: Why do asymmetric supercapacitors have higher energy density?
options: They use heavier electrode materials
Different electrode materials widen the voltage window, and energy scales with voltage squared
They operate at higher temperatures

hook.text: Fuel cells need platinum catalysts costing thousands per gram — nano engineering slashes usage by 90%.

buildup.text: Nanoparticles expose more platinum atoms on the surface — fewer grams deliver the same catalytic activity.

discovery.text: Core-shell nanoparticles put platinum only on the surface — cheap metal cores underneath carry the structure.

twist.text: Platinum nanoparticles dissolve slowly in acidic fuel cell conditions — degradation reduces lifetime and performance.

climax.text: Single-atom catalysts anchor individual platinum atoms on carbon supports — ultimate atom efficiency, zero waste.

punchline.text: Use every platinum atom — nano catalysis makes fuel cells affordable.

quiz.question: How do core-shell nanoparticles reduce platinum use in fuel cells?
options: They replace platinum with iron entirely
Platinum is placed only on the particle surface over a cheaper metal core, maximizing atom efficiency
They increase the fuel cell's operating temperature to need less catalyst

hook.text: Split water with electricity and you get hydrogen fuel — nano catalysts make the reaction faster and cheaper.

buildup.text: The oxygen evolution reaction is the bottleneck — it needs 300 mV overpotential even with the best bulk catalysts.

discovery.text: Nano-structured NiFe layered double hydroxides reduce overpotential by 100 mV — matching iridium oxide performance.

twist.text: High current densities cause bubble formation that blocks active sites — gas management is a nano-scale challenge.

climax.text: Industrial electrolyzers now use nanostructured non-precious catalysts — making green hydrogen cost-competitive.

punchline.text: Nano surfaces split water faster — turning electricity into clean hydrogen fuel.

quiz.question: How do nanostructured catalysts improve water splitting?
options: They heat the water to make it split spontaneously
They reduce the overpotential needed for the oxygen evolution reaction, improving efficiency
They filter out impurities in the water before splitting

hook.text: Sunlight plus water plus a nano catalyst equals hydrogen — solar fuel with no electricity needed.

buildup.text: Semiconductor nanoparticles absorb light and generate electron-hole pairs that drive water-splitting reactions.

discovery.text: TiO₂ nanoparticles were the first photocatalysts — but only absorb UV light, just 4% of the solar spectrum.

twist.text: Visible-light photocatalysts like g-C₃N₄ absorb more spectrum but recombine charges too fast — low efficiency.

climax.text: Z-scheme heterostructures mimic photosynthesis — two nano catalysts working in tandem boost efficiency tenfold.

punchline.text: Sunlight on a nano particle splits water into fuel — artificial photosynthesis.

quiz.question: Why is TiO₂ limited as a solar photocatalyst?
options: It dissolves in water during the reaction
It only absorbs ultraviolet light, which is just 4% of the solar spectrum
It produces oxygen instead of hydrogen

hook.text: Turn CO₂ back into fuel — nano catalysts convert the greenhouse gas into methanol, ethanol, or syngas.

buildup.text: Copper nanoparticles reduce CO₂ electrochemically — different facets produce different products selectively.

discovery.text: Oxide-derived copper nanostructures favor multi-carbon products like ethanol — higher value than simple CO or methane.

twist.text: Selectivity is still poor — a mix of products forms, and separating them costs more than the fuel is worth.

climax.text: Single-site catalysts on nano supports now achieve 90% selectivity for CO — making syngas economically viable.

punchline.text: Nano catalysts close the carbon loop — turning waste CO₂ back into fuel.

quiz.question: Why is product selectivity a challenge in CO₂ electroreduction?
options: CO₂ does not react with any metal catalyst
Multiple products form simultaneously, and separating them is costly
The reaction requires temperatures above 1000°C

hook.text: Nafion membranes conduct protons but cost 500 dollars per square meter — nano alternatives aim to slash that price.

buildup.text: Proton exchange membranes must conduct H⁺ while blocking gas crossover — a delicate nano-porous balance.

discovery.text: Nano-composite membranes with silica or zeolite fillers retain water at high temperature — boosting conductivity.

twist.text: Filler agglomeration creates gas leak paths — uniform nano-dispersion is critical but hard to achieve.

climax.text: Hydrocarbon nano-membranes now match Nafion performance at a fraction of the cost — scaling for mass market.

punchline.text: A membrane just nanometers thick decides if a fuel cell is affordable.

quiz.question: What is the role of nano-fillers in fuel cell membranes?
options: They generate electricity directly
They retain water and improve proton conductivity at high temperatures
They catalyze the hydrogen oxidation reaction

hook.text: A fuel cell powered by glucose from your blood — nano enzymes on electrodes generate electricity from body sugar.

buildup.text: Glucose oxidase immobilized on carbon nanotube electrodes converts glucose to electrons efficiently.

discovery.text: Direct electron transfer from enzyme to nanotube eliminates the need for chemical mediators — simpler design.

twist.text: Enzymes denature over days — the fuel cell loses power as proteins unfold on the electrode surface.

climax.text: Nanozymes — synthetic nanoparticles mimicking enzymes — never denature and work for months in implanted devices.

punchline.text: Your blood sugar powers a nano fuel cell — the body becomes the battery.

quiz.question: What advantage do nanozymes have over natural enzymes in biofuel cells?
options: They produce more glucose
They do not denature, maintaining function for months instead of days
They are more selective for glucose than natural enzymes

hook.text: Walk on a floor and generate electricity — ZnO nanowire arrays convert footstep pressure into power.

buildup.text: Bending a piezoelectric nanowire separates positive and negative charges — creating voltage across its length.

discovery.text: Zhong Lin Wang invented the nanogenerator in 2006 — proving nanoscale mechanical energy can be harvested usefully.

twist.text: Each nanowire generates picowatts — millions are needed in parallel for microwatt-level useful output.

climax.text: Self-powered nano sensors run on vibration energy alone — no batteries, no wires, just ambient motion.

punchline.text: Bend a nanowire and it gives you electricity — motion becomes power.

quiz.question: How do piezoelectric nanogenerators harvest energy?
options: They absorb light and convert it to electricity
Mechanical deformation of piezoelectric nanowires separates charges, generating voltage
They use magnetic fields to induce current in nanowires

hook.text: Rub two surfaces together and static charge builds — triboelectric nanogenerators harvest that friction as power.

buildup.text: Nano-textured surfaces maximize contact area and charge transfer — amplifying the triboelectric effect enormously.

discovery.text: TENGs produce high voltage at low current — perfect for directly driving sensors and small electronics.

twist.text: Humidity kills triboelectric charge — water molecules screen the surface and drain the signal.

climax.text: Waterproof TENG designs now harvest wave energy from oceans — blue energy from every passing wave.

punchline.text: Friction at nano surfaces turns any motion into usable electricity.

quiz.question: What limits triboelectric nanogenerator performance?
options: They only work in a vacuum
Humidity screens surface charge, reducing output — requiring waterproof or sealed designs
They require extremely high temperatures to operate

hook.text: Waste heat is everywhere — thermoelectric nanomaterials turn temperature differences directly into electricity.

buildup.text: The Seebeck effect drives electrons from hot to cold — creating a voltage proportional to the temperature gradient.

discovery.text: Nanostructured bismuth telluride scatters phonons at grain boundaries — cutting thermal conductivity while preserving charge flow.

twist.text: The figure of merit ZT rarely exceeds 2.5 — converting more than a few percent of heat to electricity is still hard.

climax.text: Body-heat powered wearables use flexible nano thermoelectric films — skin warmth drives health monitoring sensors.

punchline.text: Nano-grain boundaries block heat but let electrons flow — waste heat becomes power.

quiz.question: How do nanostructured thermoelectrics improve efficiency?
options: They increase thermal conductivity to move heat faster
Grain boundaries scatter phonons, reducing thermal conductivity while maintaining electrical conductivity
They convert light to heat before generating electricity

hook.text: Cool a building without electricity — nanostructured surfaces radiate heat into space through the atmosphere's IR window.

buildup.text: The atmosphere is transparent between 8 and 13 micrometers — surfaces emitting in this band lose heat to outer space.

discovery.text: Multilayer nano-photonic films are engineered to emit maximally in the sky window while reflecting all sunlight.

twist.text: On humid days the atmospheric window narrows — water vapor absorbs some of the emitted radiation, reducing cooling.

climax.text: SkyCool Systems commercialized radiative cooling panels — cutting building AC costs by 20% in California trials.

punchline.text: A nano-designed surface cools itself by beaming heat into outer space.

quiz.question: How do radiative cooling nanostructures lower temperature without electricity?
options: They absorb cold from the atmosphere
They emit infrared radiation through the atmospheric transparency window directly into outer space
They block all sunlight from reaching the surface

hook.text: Temperature fluctuations throughout the day are untapped energy — pyroelectric nanofilms harvest every swing.

buildup.text: Pyroelectric materials generate current when temperature changes — not from a gradient, but from the rate of change.

discovery.text: PVDF nanofiber mats have high pyroelectric coefficients — flexible films that generate power from thermal cycling.

twist.text: Constant temperature produces zero output — the harvester only works during transitions, not steady states.

climax.text: Coupled pyro-piezoelectric nanogenerators harvest both heat swings and vibrations — dual-mode energy scavenging.

punchline.text: Every temperature swing is wasted energy — a nano film captures it.

quiz.question: How do pyroelectric nanogenerators differ from thermoelectric ones?
options: They generate power from the rate of temperature change, not a static temperature gradient
They require higher temperatures to operate
They only work in a vacuum

topics.title: RF Energy Harvesting with Nano Antennas

hook.text: WiFi, cell signals, and FM radio fill the air — nano rectennas can harvest this ambient RF energy.

buildup.text: A rectenna is an antenna coupled to a rectifier — it converts radio waves directly into DC electricity.

discovery.text: Carbon nanotube-based rectennas operate at optical frequencies — potentially harvesting light as electricity directly.

twist.text: Ambient RF power density is microwatts per square meter — harvesting meaningful energy requires large collection areas.

climax.text: MIT demonstrated a flexible rectenna that powers a small LED from WiFi signals — wireless power from thin air.

punchline.text: Radio waves already surround us — nano antennas turn them into power.

quiz.question: What is a rectenna?
options: A rectangular antenna used for television
An antenna coupled to a rectifier that converts radio waves directly into DC electricity
A nanotube that stores radio wave energy as heat
